transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated. It happens in client interviews, tutoring sessions, even at book club. I’ll just get up, and people are starting to notice I can’t seem to sit and listen for very long.
Did you experience this kind of restlessness or difficulty staying seated when you were a child?

Yes. My grade-school report cards always said I was bright, but couldn’t stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother still jokes that I treated every classroom like a crime scene I needed to pace through.
Aside from feeling restless, do you have trouble sustaining your attention or staying focused on tasks?
I’m not really sure. I’ve noticed the getting-up part more than anything else. What do you mean by trouble focusing?
For example, do you often find yourself getting easily distracted or sidetracked when trying to work on a task?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself getting sidetracked while I’m working. The main thing I’ve noticed is needing to get up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with prominent symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity, specifically an inability to remain seated in settings where it is expected (e.g., meetings, tutoring sessions, book club) and difficulty waiting their turn, with documented onset dating back to elementary school. Inattentive symptoms were queried and denied or not observed. This clinical presentation meets criteria for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, predominantly hyperactive/impulsive presentation (ICD-10-CM F90.1).
